title: review: R5: orchestrator/sched_scorecard.py — scheduling scorecard: predicted vs actual interference, stale outcomes, duration error, queue time and heuristic validation (AP P14)
spec:
Why: waves.jsonl records predicted interference and priorities (daemon.dispatch wave_row: ready, running, baseline_order, wave, deferred, predicted [{a,b,level,reasons}], priority {tid: critical_path.explain}, applied), stale.jsonl records stale checks, dispatch.jsonl records skip reasons, and merge.merge fails tasks with reason rebase_conflict — but nothing joins predictions to outcomes, so the heuristics are unvalidated (AP P14; brief P9).
What: new pure module orchestrator/sched_scorecard.py reading via schedlog.read_with_malformed and the tasks dir under root; no daemon edits.
- pair_outcomes(root) -> rows per predicted pair {a, b, level, predicted_reasons, both_ran_concurrently (both dispatched before either gated), actual_conflict (either task later reason rebase_conflict / hold merge conflict / stale row action rebase_conflict), stale_event (stale row risk high for either), fix_round (any fix-round child via constraints.fix_round_for), serialized (pair appeared in deferred with hard:/soft: reason)}.
- task_outcomes(root) -> per execute task {queue_wait_s (dispatched_at - first_ready_at or created), predicted_duration_s (from the latest waves row priority[tid].est_duration_s), actual_duration_s (duration.actual_s), error (duration.prediction_error), critical_path_s (priority), accepted (merged_into set), fix_rounds, total_tokens/usd from runs rows for the task lineage when present}.
- build(root=STATE) -> card {"hard_conflict_precision": conflicts among concurrently-run hard-predicted pairs / such pairs or None, "soft_conflict_usefulness": conflict rate of concurrently-run soft pairs vs none-level pairs, "unnecessary_serialization": serialized pairs whose tasks' changed files (task.changed_files or scope literals) were disjoint / serialized pairs, "conflict_rate", "stale_work_rate", "duration_mape" and n, "median_queue_wait_s", "goal_latency_s" per goal from tasks (min created to max merged), "accepted_cost_usd" sum, "n_waves", "n_pairs", "malformed"}; None for undefined metrics, never a fabricated 0.
- format(card) -> text table; every metric line shows n.
Depends on R1 duration.actual_s/prediction_error (import orchestrator.duration).
acceptance: tests/test_sched_scorecard.py::test_predicted_hard_pair_that_conflicted_counts_toward_precision — a waves row predicting hard for (A,B), both dispatched concurrently, B later failed rebase_conflict: hard_conflict_precision 1.0 with n 1
tests/test_sched_scorecard.py::test_stale_outcomes_are_attributed_to_pairs_and_rate — stale rows with risk high for a predicted pair set stale_event True and stale_work_rate reflects it

tests/test_sched_scorecard.py::test_duration_prediction_error_uses_priority_estimate_and_actual — predicted 1200 s, actual 600 s yields per-task error ratio 2.0 and duration_mape over tasks with both values

tests/test_sched_scorecard.py::test_malformed_telemetry_is_tolerated_and_counted — broken lines in waves.jsonl and stale.jsonl are skipped, card.malformed counts them, undefined metrics are None not 0
tests/test_sched_scorecard.py::test_unnecessary_serialization_detects_disjoint_deferred_pairs — a soft-deferred pair whose changed files were disjoint counts as unnecessary serialization 1.0

result.summary: Ran the full test_sched_scorecard.py suite (7 tests, including all 5 named acceptance tests) against HEAD 7a6ac55: all pass. Traced pair_outcomes/task_outcomes/build logic by hand for each acceptance scenario (hard-conflict precision, stale attribution, duration MAPE via duration.actual_s/prediction_error, malformed-line tolerance via schedlog.read_with_malformed, disjoint-file serialization detection) and confirmed the computed values match expected results (e.g. ratio 2.0, precision 1.0/n=1, malformed=2, undefined metrics return None not 0). Scope is respected — only orchestrator/sched_scorecard.py and tests/test_sched_scorecard.py touched, no daemon edits. Noted but not flagging: _sched_rows temporarily mutates the module-global schedlog.SCHED_DIR under a local lock that daemon.py's schedlog.append() doesn't share, which would be a real race only if this scorecard build were invoked concurrently in-process with the daemon (it's normally a separate CLI invocation, so not a practical issue). No security concerns — module only reads local task/JSONL files, no external input or shell/network calls.
